The failure is that the RM encodes the wrong property. The task is G(has_door_key -> F door_open) AND F target_picked_up: EVERY moment spent holding the key must find the door open at that moment or see it opened afterwards, and only then the box. The candidate encodes only an existential ordered chain F(has_door_key) then F(door_open) then F(target_picked_up): it monitors exactly one key-holding episode (the first) and then goes deaf. Per the environment spec, door_open is a reversible condition ('false again if toggled shut'; only relocking is forbidden), so an obligation can arise after the RM has already reached u2 and the candidate's u2 else-loop never sees it. Concrete violating trace that earns the full 1.2 under the candidate: pick up the ball, pick up the key, unlock and enter the far room carrying the key, drop the key there, toggle the door shut from the far side, pick the key back up (has_door_key true, door_open false -- a live obligation), drop it (key_lost fires, door closed), pick up the box. Every environment constraint is respected (target_picked_up still occurs after a prior door_open; has_door_key and target_picked_up never co-occur), the task's whenever-clause is violated (the door is closed at that later holding and never opened afterwards), yet the candidate transitions u2->u3 and pays 1.0. The same blind spot makes the RM miss any post-opening key-holding with a shut door, even when the episode then times out. A faithful machine needs ongoing obligation tracking, not a one-shot chain: states distinguishing 'no pending obligation' from 'obligation pending (key held with the door closed since the last opening)', discharge only on door_open from the pending state, explicit persistence of the obligation through key_lost and through re-pickups while the door is closed, no obligation created when the key is picked up while the door is already open, and the target_picked_up transition to the accepting state allowed only from the no-pending state (box pickup with an obligation pending must fall into a non-accepting sink, since the episode ends there and 'opened afterwards' can no longer occur). Also note the step where the door opens necessarily co-occurs with has_door_key (unlocking requires the key in hand); the transition design must not let a has_door_key-labeled edge steal the discharge step or create a spurious obligation on a pickup that happens while the door is open. As written, the candidate is the RM for the simpler task 'get the key, open the door, pick up the box', not for the given whenever-obligation task; reject and regenerate with explicit regression/obligation handling.
